entry_disclaimer.title: New molecular and imaging findings
entry_disclaimer.body: Liquid biopsies (April–May 2026) have revealed new alterations: ESR1 D538G (endocrine resistance) and RB1 mutations (a predictor of neuroendocrine transition). The Ga-68 DOTATOC PET-CT confirms multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor overexpression (SSTR+) — a new therapeutic target via radioligand therapy (PRRT). The molecular profile has become more complex and reinforces the need to explore the neuroendocrine pathway in parallel with the luminal one.

home.intro_line: Diagnosed in March 2026 with luminal breast cancer and a neuroendocrine component that does not fit standard protocols.
home.s3_heading: What Spanish protocols don't cover, we cover.
home.s3_subheading: Spanish protocols only account for half of the tumor's biology: they're built for standard HR+ breast cancer, and Miriam's is not.
home.s3_p1: Histologically it is a luminal breast carcinoma (HR+/HER2−). But IHC detected ~80% neuroendocrine differentiation. That second biology is not part of the standard Spanish protocol.
home.s3_p2: Practical result: hormonal treatment covers the luminal component. The neuroendocrine component, with its own dynamics and targets, is left unaddressed.
home.s3_p3: Oncologists cannot prescribe off-protocol without solid evidence. Generating that evidence requires molecular rebiopsy, advanced panels and international review boards. None of this is funded by public healthcare for a low-frequency case.
home.s3_pet_paragraph: Gallium-68 DOTATOC PET-CT: multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor overexpression (SSTR+) and focal uptake in the right breast tail. The tumor expresses a target that breast protocols do not contemplate as standard, opening the radioligand path (Lu-177 / Ac-225).

home.s6_quote: My tumor doesn't fit any protocol. Treating it well means mapping the whole thing —the luminal side and the possible neuroendocrine side— and designing the treatment on that data, not on the average of other patients.
home.s6_outro: Miriam isn't asking for a miracle. She's asking that the precision medicine that already exists reach her case before the available options shrink.
home.s8_heading: The goal is an N-of-1 trial designed for this tumor's exact biology.
home.s8_p1: An {nof1} trial is a clinical trial built for a single patient: treatment is designed around her tumor's actual profile, not an average protocol. That makes it possible to combine drugs to target both of her pathways at once — the luminal and the possible neuroendocrine one.
home.s8_advantages_title: The advantages of reaching that trial:

Drugs suited to each part of the tumor can be applied simultaneously.
Every result obtained contributes evidence for other patients with similar profiles.
Miriam stops depending on a single protocol that does not answer her case.

ciencia.proposed_panel_caption: Proposed rebiopsy panel: components, methods, targets and clinical implication
ciencia.goal_n_of_1_desc: A clinical trial with one patient. Therapeutic decisions are designed on the tumor's actual molecular profile, not on a generic HR+ average. The path: rebiopsy with advanced panel → review at WIN Consortium international MTB → molecularly-directed N-of-1 treatment.
ciencia.win_consortium_desc: WIN Consortium (Worldwide Innovative Network in Oncology) connects precision-oncology centres of excellence to design individualised diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
ciencia.win_consortium_precedent: A precedent: precision oncology decided on the patient's molecular data, not on the tumor's label.
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines: Why doesn't this tumor fit the protocols?
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines_text: On paper this is a luminal breast cancer (HR+/HER2−). Under the microscope, ~80% of the tumor shows neuroendocrine differentiation, with FGFR1 ×13 and CCND1 ×20 amplification. Protocols recommend treating it as standard luminal and ignoring the neuroendocrine component. Clinical literature shows this hybrid subtype (BC-NED) has worse prognosis and usually needs different strategies.
ciencia.thesis: The thesis: biology, not the organ of origin, should guide treatment.
ciencia.thesis_goal: Goal: an N-of-1 trial that sets a precedent for precision oncology in ultra-rare subtypes.
ciencia.updates_2026_subtitle: Results generated in 2026 that complement the 2024 primary-tissue profile.
ciencia.ctdna_what: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from peripheral blood analyzed by NGS. A standard blood draw detects mutations, amplifications and clonal dynamics without a tissue biopsy. Especially useful in bone-only disease, where tissue is scarce or molecularly uninformative.
ciencia.imaging_what: PET with the 68Ga-DOTATOC radiotracer, which binds somatostatin receptors (SSTR). Visualizes in vivo which lesions express SSTR and could therefore respond to radioligand therapy (PRRT).

team.title: The team
team.subtitle: One patient, an international team, and artificial intelligence searching for the therapy that conventional oncology doesn't consider.
team.how_it_formed: This team wasn't planned. It formed organically when professionals from different fields (technology, medicine, AI, research) saw a case that challenged them and decided to contribute what they knew. There is no formal hierarchy. There is a shared goal: let this tumor's biology guide treatment.

historia.pending_notice: This section is being written by someone close to Miriam. It will tell her story from before the diagnosis: who she is beyond cancer, how she got here, and why what she's doing matters. Coming soon.
historia.story_teaser_1: Three years ago, Miriam was working full-time as a software developer and creating content about technology. Within a matter of months, her life took a radical turn.
historia.story_teaser_2: It all began with back pain, physiotherapy sessions and GPs who couldn't find a solution. As the pain persisted and she wasn't getting answers, she decided to arrange an MRI scan herself. One Thursday in January 2024, she found the test results in her inbox: “probable vertebral metastases”. A couple of weeks later, the definitive diagnosis arrived: “Stage IV breast cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation”.
historia.story_teaser_3: For two years, Miriam has been rebuilding her life piece by piece with treatments that have given her time and peace of mind, but with an end date. In 2026, everything has moved forward at breakneck speed. What if these advances, combined with the specific nature of her cancer, opened doors that previously seemed closed?
historia.story_teaser_4: In this story, we want to tell you about Miriam's case, her journey and her daily routine so that you can truly understand what it means to live with stage 4 cancer.

collaborate.profile5_text: You don't have to contribute anything. If knowing this case exists and is openly documented helps, it already serves its purpose. To share yours or contact Miriam, write by email or DM. She replies personally when she can.
notus_list: We are not a patients' association. We are a volunteer team focused on a specific case.
We do not promise cures. We document biological hypotheses and their real probabilities.
We do not use “fight” or “warrior” language. We talk biology, data and clinical decisions.
We do not replace the medical team. We add external analysis; clinical decisions are signed by Miriam's oncology team.
We do not publish clinical data without review. Transparency demands rigor, not speed.
collaborate.links_sub: If you don't know where to start, share helpmiriam.com. Getting the case in front of the right oncologist, researcher or patient is often the difference between finding a therapeutic target and not finding one.
